title: After Wikimania Paris 2026, I see Wikipedia in a different light
content: Previously, I had attended several Wikimedia events in the ESEAP (East, Southeast Asia, and Pacific) region, such as the ESEAP Conference in Kota Kinabalu in 2024 and the ESEAP Strategy Summit 2025. At the ESEAP Conference in Kota Kinabalu, I was only familiar with the Kent Wiki Club, which is part of the Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia. Therefore, I wasn’t entirely sure what my role would be. However, with the help of the organizers—and since Kota Kinabalu was the host city—I participated as a translator for the Kadazandusun language. At that time, I was grateful to have received full sponsorship. Similarly, at the 2025 ESEAP Strategy Summit held in Manila, I mostly served as an observer. Back then, I still felt shy and lacked the confidence to approach others. I had many questions I wanted to ask, but sometimes shyness made me choose to just listen. I saw the Wikimedia community as a large one, with many experienced contributors. I admired the passion of the Wikimedians, but I still felt small within that community. However, Wikimania Paris 2026 provided a different experience.

title: Two weekends in June: Wikimedia Ukraine’s forum for administrators and patrollers
content:
On 20 and 27 June 2026, Wikimedia Ukraine held a forum for Ukrainian Wikipedia’s administrators and patrollers – one day online, one day in-person in Kyiv. Around 30 people took part across the two weekends: about 20 joined the online day, 18 came to Kyiv, and a few did both.

It was our second such event after an online forum in 2021 – and the first one since we’ve launched a full-fledged program of support for users with extended rights. Here’s a brief look at how the forum came about and how it looked like.

Ukrainian Wikipedia has around 50 administrators and around 600 patrollers – the volunteers who review incoming edits, revert vandalism, close deletion discussions and generally keep the encyclopedia reliable. Their job has not been getting easier, partly because of pressures the whole movement shares and partly because of ones specific to Ukraine under Russia’s military invasion.

title: Reflections from Wikimania Paris 2026
content:
You could be a Wikimedian all your life, editing in your small corner of the world, but nothing beats being in the same space with over a thousand fellow Wikimedians who have flown, trained and travelled from every corner of the world.

Being in that space, the realisation that this is beyond clicking some keys on your keyboard and pressing the publish button hit me so hard. This was a movement. I had always known it was a movement, but never had I ever seen it so clearly as I did during Wikimania 2026 in Paris.

title: My Virtual Wikimania 2026 Experience: Reflecting on learning, community, and the future of free knowledge
content:
Although I attended Wikimania 2026 virtually from Uganda, I still felt connected to the global Wikimedia community. As the movement celebrated 25 years, the conference brought together Wikimedians, researchers, educators, and partners from across the world to exchange ideas and shape the future of free knowledge.

Uganda had a strong presence at this year’s conference, with five participants(Micheal Kaluba, Sandra Aceng, Brian Baluku, Geofrey Kateregga, and Ssemanda Will) attending in person in Paris and twenty of us joining online. While participating virtually was a different experience from being onsite, it still provided an opportunity to learn from experts, follow important discussions, and engage with the wider Wikimedia movement.

title: Announcing and Exploring DCW’s Digital Certification Portal: the difference it makes
content:
Deoband Community Wikimedia turned 5 on 31 July 2026, and over the past five years, we have heard differently about how the student and Gen Z community can be retained in our ecosystem of knowledge production. We thus built the Digital Certification Portal, publicly live at certificates.dcwwiki.org 

DCW’s Digital Certification Portal is the 5th-anniversary gift from its volunteers to support retention. Initially designed to issue certificates of participation for our Wikiversary Conference in February 2026, it very soon moved to a full-fledged application with several advanced functions. 

The portal is a very lightweight and monolithic PHP application for bulk-generating and distributing verifiable event and program participation certificates (public claim + verification). Organisers use the admin dashboard to upload PDF templates, map dynamic fields, import participants via CSV or add them manually, generate certificates (PDF), and send notifications; end users claim or verify certificates via the public UI. The different story here is that we are not relying on any paid APIs or using any extensive third-party tools like Credly in this process.

title: Wiki Loves Uzbek Cinema:A Cross-Border Collaboration with Wikimedia Czech Republic
content:
During my participation in the CEE Wiki Peer Learning Exchange Program, one of my key goals was to discover new project formats that could inspire and energize the Uzbek Wikipedia community. That inspiration found its perfect match during my exchanges with the Wikimedia Czech Republic team, specifically around their ongoing Wiki Loves Film initiative.

While WMCZ has been successfully hosting this campaign since 2024, Uzbekistan had never participated before. Seeing the potential of this project, I reached out to Pavel Bednařík for advice and guidance. Together, we agreed to launch an edit-a-thon titled “Wiki Loves Uzbek Cinema” on July 14, marking Uzbekistan’s debut in the movement. Inspired by our discussions, I set to work on our local community platform:

  • Created the dedicated Wiki Loves Film project page on Uzbek Wikipedia.
  • Curated a targeted list of recommended articles on Meta-Wiki focusing on Uzbek cinema history, notable films, and filmmakers.

title: Celebrating Africa’s Rich Cultural Heritage Through Open Knowledge: Culture Connect Africa 2026 in the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group
content:
Africa’s cultural heritage is one of the richest in the world. Its films tell powerful stories, its festivals preserve centuries-old traditions, and its cuisine reflects the diversity of its people. Yet much of this knowledge remains underrepresented on Wikimedia platforms. To help bridge this gap, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group collaborated with African & Proud (AP), the organizers of the Culture Connect Africa 2026 project, to document and celebrate African culture through open knowledge.

Running from May to August 2026, the campaign empowered volunteers to create and improve Wikipedia and Wikidata content related to African film, festivals, cuisine, and travel. Through training sessions, edit-a-thons, and friendly competitions, contributors worked together to ensure that more of Africa’s stories are freely accessible to people around the world.

Culture Connect Africa 2026 was organized into monthly campaigns, each focusing on a different aspect of African cultural heritage.

title: ESEAP Conference 2026: Japanese Contributor Experiences (Part 1)
content:
This article presents—in two parts—the experiences of 13 Japanese Wikimedians who attended the ESEAP Conference 2026, held in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, from May 15 to 17, 2026. Eight of the 13 were first-time attendees, including three students. The group was diverse, spanning ages from the teens to the seventies and featuring an equal gender split; each contributor shared their experience from their own unique perspective. This marked the third time Japanese contributors attended an ESEAP event, following the 2024 Conference and the 2025 Strategy Summit, and the Strategy Summit is scheduled to be held in Japan next year.

Ezokomachi：I first learned about ESEAP when I contributed in a local edit-a-thon last year. Although I had never taken part in an international Wikipedia event before, I decided to join because I wanted to know what Wikimedians active in the same Asian region were thinking and doing.

Norimaki：Having been active on the Japanese Wikipedia for about twenty years, I decided to contribute in an international event because I wanted to experience firsthand what such gatherings are like.

title: Beyond the Photograph: The Eiffel Tower, Open Knowledge, and Human Experiences
content:
One of the highlights of my Wikimania experience was taking an evening to visit the Eiffel Tower. Standing there and seeing the Eiffel Tower in all its glory felt surreal. I had seen countless pictures and videos of it before, but being physically present was a completely different experience. There is something special about encountering a place, an artefact, or a cultural moment in real life. Being physically present allows us to experience the atmosphere, emotions, and unexpected moments that surround it.

At the same time, not everyone will have the opportunity to visit every museum, landmark, or cultural site in person. This is where digitisation plays an important role. It creates pathways for more people to discover, learn, and connect with culture in ways that may not have been possible before.
